title: Liturgical Calendar Validations Path
description: The source data this API can be asked to validate. Clients iterate this list and send back an item's opaque id, so no filesystem path crosses the wire.

id.description: Opaque identifier a client sends back to request this check.

region.description: Null when the item applies to its whole rite; an ISO nation code when it applies only to that nation's calendar.

schema.description: Bare filename of the JSON schema this item validates against, resolvable under /schemas.

steps.description: The ordered checks this item passes through when validated. A frame's own `step` field carries these same values (`exists`, `parses`, `validates`), plus a fourth, `complete`, that marks the terminal frame and is not a check. Read `step` on each frame to know what it is about; stop watching a check when a frame arrives whose `step` is `complete`, not when you have counted `steps.length` frames. The terminal `complete` frame is sent only in reply to a request that carried a `requestId`: it is a new frame rather than a new field, so it is gated on the v2 opt-in signal to keep a frame-counting v1 client from miscounting. A client that stops on `complete` must send a `requestId` on every request. Every arm of a source-data check emits exactly one frame per entry in this array, whatever the outcome and wherever it stops: a file that is absent, or that does not decode, reports the steps it never got to as failed rather than leaving them unsent, since a step a client is never told about and a step that passed are indistinguishable to it. So the length is a reliable count of the frames to expect, and is safe to size a rendering with -- one card per step. It is still not what you should wait on: stop on `complete`, which stays correct for an arm that some later change makes shorter. Pair that with a timeout rather than waiting unboundedly: the guarantee is that every request which starts work terminates, and it has a known hole while https://github.com/Liturgical-Calendar/LiturgicalCalendarAPI/issues/823 is open -- a throw inside a promise fulfilment handler skips the terminal frame, and a queued request dropped when a run is superseded is discarded without one. See https://github.com/Liturgical-Calendar/LiturgicalCalendarAPI/issues/821, which is where the decode arm's missing `validates` frame was fixed, and https://github.com/Liturgical-Calendar/LiturgicalCalendarAPI/issues/822, where an absent file stopped being reported as present. See https://github.com/Liturgical-Calendar/LiturgicalCalendarAPI/issues/819, closed by this work: these step names now reach the wire as the frame's own `step` field, so there is no second vocabulary left to relate them to.

expected_locales.description: The locales this item's folder is expected to hold a `{locale}.json` for. Non-null exactly when `steps` contains `covers`. Null for file items, and for a folder whose owner's declared locales are scanned from that very folder -- a wider region's and a missal's `i18n` -- where the comparison would be a tautology. A national or diocesan `i18n` folder is not null: those calendars declare `locales` in their own source file, so the expectation has an authority independent of what the folder happens to contain. The comparison is a subset test by locale identity, never by count: a declared locale with no file fails the `covers` step, while a file for a locale the owner does not declare does not fail it and is named in the frame text instead.
